name: Dien Bien Phu food guide
summary: Eat at the Thái table: pa pỉnh tộp folded and grilled over charcoal, chicken in lemongrass leaves, twice-steamed upland sticky rice, and everything dipped in chẩm chéo. Spring brings ban flower from the passes, and the kitchen fire gives buffalo dried in its smoke.
body: The meal to come for is a Thái house table in the basin, at bản Phiêng Lơi near the city entrance when a family is receiving guests. The fish is split, stuffed with mắc khén and herbs, and grilled whole, and the sticky rice comes as a ball you eat by hand. Sơn La is the hearth across Pha Đin, and Mộc Châu is the yogurt morning further east.

Black chicken belongs to Tủa Chùa, and rau ban to March and April on the passes. Duck with banana flower cooks about three hours in banana leaves, so it is a family dish for guests rather than a street plate.

Hearth-dried meat, buffalo, pork, or beef, comes off the fire red and still hot. Kitchen-smoked buffalo hangs longer: Vietnam News describes about 15 hours of smoke, and Vietnamnet a 2–3 hour marinade, a slow charcoal dry, and a 30-minute resteam. Hương Linh – Tủa Chùa tea and Mường Ảng coffee are the provincial products to take home.
specialtiesLead: Start with the Thái table, then the tám rice, the hearth, and the provincial specialities to ask a host about.

sections.heading: City specialties
paragraphs: Twenty-three plates, sauces, rice dishes, and drinks from the Thái and Mông tables. For the last four, ask your host how they are cooked.

spots.name: Pa pinh top
spots.address: Bản Phiêng Lơi, at the city entrance
spots.note: Eat it straight from the grill at a Thái table, with chẩm chéo on the side.

spots.name: Cay pinh
spots.address: A Thái hamlet that receives guests
spots.note: Hamlets that receive guests grill it at the fire and pour a cup of rice wine alongside.

spots.name: Upland sticky rice
spots.note: Eat it with grilled fish or pork, or carry a packet, cóong xôi, for the road.

spots.name: Steamed black chicken
spots.note: A Tủa Chùa dish; the same bird is also roasted with hạt dổi or cooked in a hotpot or porridge.

spots.name: Ban flower
spots.note: Look for it in March and April, when the ban flowers on the passes.

spots.name: Bitter bamboo
spots.note: The bitterness is the point: this bamboo is not soaked in salt, so the grilled shoot keeps its bitter, astringent edge.

spots.name: Pork grilled in leaves
spots.note: A Thái plate; eat it hot, straight from the leaf.

spots.name: Bon soup
spots.note: A home and hamlet soup for the Thái table.

spots.name: Hearth-dried meat
spots.note: It keeps well, so it is eaten warm with rice or carried on the road.

spots.name: Kitchen-smoked buffalo
spots.note: Some cooks smoke it for about 15 hours; others dry it more briefly over charcoal and resteam it for half an hour.

spots.name: Duck with banana flower
spots.note: Families cook it for guests, adding garlic chives, mint, and coriander near the end.

spots.name: Cabbage-wrapped oleaster
spots.note: Eat it as a wrap, with chẩm chéo on the side.

spots.name: Cham cheo
spots.note: Dip sticky rice, grilled fish, forest meat, boiled bamboo, or cabbage-wrapped oleaster in it.

spots.name: Sau chit
spots.note: Order it as the steeped wine or as porridge.

spots.name: Muong Thanh tam rice
spots.note: The same grain makes khẩu cắm, khẩu háng, and khẩu papa.

spots.name: Banh day
spots.note: A Tết cake; look for it at the new year.

spots.name: Khau cam
spots.note: Made from the tám rice of the Mường Thanh fields.

spots.name: Khau hang
spots.note: The double steaming starts with the grain still in its husk.

spots.name: Khau papa
spots.note: Made from the tám rice of the Mường Thanh fields.

spots.name: Bamboo worms
spots.note: Ask your host how they are cooked that day.

spots.name: Mong wine
spots.note: Ask your host what it is made from and how strong it is.

spots.name: Mountain goat
spots.note: Ask your host which cut is on and how it is cooked.

spots.name: Da River fish
spots.note: Ask which fish came in and how it is cooked.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: Phố đi bộ Mường Thanh is the river street, Chợ Trung tâm I is the wholesale hall, and bản Phiêng Lơi is a hamlet table rather than a stall row. The 2012 night market on Nguyễn Chí Thanh is a separate street.

spots.name: Muong Thanh walking street
spots.address: Beside the Nậm Rốm, phường Điện Biên Phủ
spots.note: The walking street beside the Nậm Rốm fills during Ban flower week; outside it, a few drink stalls at the head of the street are the stop. One trader opens weekday afternoons and evenings, and through the day at weekends.

spots.name: Central Market I
spots.address: Old phường Tân Thanh, now phường Điện Biên Phủ
spots.note: The city's wholesale market hall, opened in 1992 with about 150 kiosks.

spots.name: Nguyen Chi Thanh night market
spots.nameVi: Phố chợ đêm Nguyễn Chí Thanh
spots.address: Nguyễn Chí Thanh, as printed in 2012
spots.note: In 2012 a night market ran daily 20:00–23:30 along Nguyễn Chí Thanh, from the Trần Đăng Ninh junction to the provincial youth-house crossing. Ask locally whether it still opens.

spots.name: Ban Phieng Loi
spots.note: A Thái hamlet at the city entrance where houses serve the Thái meal to guests, and a food stop during the flower festival.

seoTitle: Dien Bien Phu food guide — the Thái table, not Sơn La
seoDescription: Pa pỉnh tộp, chicken in lemongrass leaves, twice-steamed sticky rice, kitchen-smoked buffalo, and chẩm chéo: what to eat at the Thái table in Dien Bien Phu.
